equations.meaning: A violence potential: a nonlinear functional mapping latent stress state to overt instability. Observed violent events are threshold crossings of V, not primary ontological units.

Linearization around a metastable configuration, yielding a generator Lτ dependent on memory time.

equations.text: s(t) = Σ_k c_k e^{−λ_k t} r_k
equations.meaning: Spectral decomposition of the solution; for τ > 0 the spectrum generically contains slow modes (Re(λ_k) ≈ 0+) encoding long-lived configurations of instability.

equations.label: Theorem (No-Go for Elimination by Suppression)
equations.text: Given Lτ with τ > 0, assuming (i) at least one slow spectral mode exists, (ii) suppression acts only on state amplitudes, and (iii) environmental load has nonzero time-average, then no bounded force-based intervention can drive the system to a globally violence-free absorbing state. (Proof sketch: finite memory implies non-Markovian evolution; slow modes ensure metastability; suppression does not modify Lτ so the invariant spectral structure persists; sustained load re-populates slow modes with probability one.)
equations.meaning: A structural, not normative, no-go result: force-based/suppression-only elimination of violence is generically impossible in a finite-causal-memory system under sustained load.
Generator for a minimal two-coupled-subsystem model, s1 (physical) and s2 (digital/psychological).
Eigenvalues of the two-subsystem generator; for small ε one mode becomes slow, and suppressing s1 transfers instability to s2, demonstrating recurrence and mutation without introducing new causes.
One of four operator-level modifications for durable violence reduction, corresponding to restorative justice.
